summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of TCS's upcoming Q1FY27 results and dividend, along with relevant tax information for Indian investors. However, there are a few inaccuracies regarding the TDS threshold for resident individuals and the specific section for NRI dividend taxation.

claims.claim: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is set to announce its Q1FY27 financial results on July 9, 2026.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm TCS board meeting on July 9, 2026, to consider Q1FY27 results and interim dividend.

claims.claim: The previous quarter (Q4FY26) saw a 12.22% increase in net profit, even as the stock experienced some decline.
claims.note: TCS reported a consolidated net profit increase of 12.22% for the quarter ended March 2026 (Q4FY26).

claims.claim: Dividends received from Indian companies are taxable in the hands of the recipient. This means that any dividend income you receive from TCS will be added to your total income for the financial year and taxed according to your applicable income tax slab rates.
claims.note: From FY 2020-21 onwards, dividends are taxable in the hands of the shareholders and added to their total income, taxed at applicable slab rates.

claims.claim: Companies are generally required to deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on dividend payments if the dividend amount exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year for resident individuals, as per Section 194 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: For resident individuals, the TDS threshold for dividends under Section 194 was revised to ₹10,000 from FY 2025-26.

claims.claim: For Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), the tax treatment can be different, often subject to double taxation avoidance agreements (DTAA) between India and their country of residence. NRIs generally face a TDS deduction at a rate of 20% (plus surcharge and cess) on dividend income, unless a lower rate is specified under an applicable DTAA.
claims.note: NRIs generally face a 20% TDS on dividend income, which can be lower based on DTAA.

claims.claim: Companies are generally required to deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on dividend payments if the dividend amount exceeds ₹5,000 in a financial year for resident individuals, as per Section 194 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: Section 194 applies to dividends paid to resident shareholders. For NRIs, Section 195 of the Income Tax Act applies.

article_title: TCS Q1FY27 Results & Interim Dividend: What Investors Need to Know
